title: Red Saunders, the Club DeLisa and Ike Day
summary: Jones recalls Red Saunders bringing Lester to the Club DeLisa in 1936 and calls Ike Day one of the greatest drummers.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: That's right. Then he took charge of all the little boys. He took care of everybody. Lester Young... had gotten Red Saunders from the West Side to bring him to

Red Saunders. He was a father confessor and out of that you had one of the greatest drummers that ever lived in the jazz world, Ike Day. Nobody has ever and ever will play that much drums. No, they won't play as much as him.
He got wasted along the way, didn't he?
Well, we've all - you know, we all do what we do. He was the greatest.
